items.title: MemToC: Benchmarking Memory-Tool Conflict Resolution in Large Language Models
items.title_zh: MemToC：大语言模型记忆—工具冲突消解基准
items.summary: MemToC is a controlled benchmark for post-tool-return arbitration built from 6,504 evaluation episodes, 542 quality-controlled factual questions, model-specific closed-book answers and tool returns of known correctness, instantiating four source-correctness cases. Across five open-weight 7–9B models tool returns strongly dominate parametric memory: instruction-tuned models retain a verified-correct answer against an incorrect tool in only 6.5–17.1% of eligible cases, follow a correct tool in 86.0–93.1%, and no cross-model ordering is stable across three instruction-wording variants.

items.title: Co-Evolving Structured Knowledge and Reasoning in Language Models
items.title_zh: 语言模型中结构化知识与推理的协同演化
items.summary: KBevo is a co-evolving framework that jointly learns to construct a structured knowledge base and reason over it for knowledge-intensive question answering, optimizing both components end-to-end with QA outcome rewards so that reasoning success directly improves the constructed knowledge base. The authors report larger, better-connected knowledge structures with higher answer reachability, plus improved compositional factual reasoning and controllability compared with standard retrieval baselines.

items.title: The Hugging Face incident and the road ahead
items.title_zh: Hugging Face 事件及其后续之路
items.summary: OpenAI shares findings from the Hugging Face security incident and outlines steps it is taking to strengthen AI model security, monitoring and alignment.

items.title: Don't Overthink, Don't Underthink: Toward Adaptive Reasoning in Agentic AI
items.title_zh: 别过度思考，也别思考不足：迈向智能体 AI 的自适应推理
items.summary: The paper argues that fixed or pre-allocated reasoning controls suit agentic systems poorly because reasoning demands evolve through planning, tool use, memory retrieval and agent-to-agent interaction, characterizing over-reasoning and under-reasoning as recurring failure modes of misallocated reasoning. On MATH-500 and the GAIA public validation set, over-reasoning cases incur higher computational cost without proportional accuracy gains, while under-reasoning cases are consistently associated with incorrect or incomplete solutions.

items.title: Assessing mentalization in humans and large language models
items.title_zh: 评估人类与大语言模型的心理化能力
items.summary: The study uses two economic games with cognitive computational modeling to uncover latent mentalization strategies in LLM agents from four model families (DeepSeek, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 and Gemini 2.0 Flash; N = 2,099), benchmarked against 251 human participants. LLMs showed behavioural and computational signatures of mentalizing that differed by provider and size, strategic prompting generally improved performance, and GPT-5 agents adapted their recursive depth of reasoning to opponent sophistication, outperforming human participants.

items.title: MoganColBERT-TR: A Late-Interaction Multi-Vector Retrieval Model for Turkish
items.title_zh: MoganColBERT-TR：面向土耳其语的晚期交互多向量检索模型
items.summary: MoganColBERT-TR is a Turkish multi-vector retrieval model that represents queries and documents at the token level through a 768→128 projection and MaxSim late interaction, initialized from the MoganBERT-TR embedding encoder and adapted with single-epoch distillation from a cross-encoder teacher. With 148.9M parameters it scores 37.36 overall (35.53 nDCG@100, 31.81 nDCG@10) across five zero-shot Turkish BEIR datasets, beating the twice-as-large ColmmBERT-base-TR on four of five datasets and finishing second among five compared models.

items.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
items.title_zh: AsymSpec：面向智能体 LLM 的上下文非对称推测解码
items.summary: AsymSpec is an asymmetric speculative decoding framework in which a lightweight drafter reads the full input while a large verifier operates on a compressed context, with contrastive δ-fusion of logits and a divergence-aware acceptance gate to keep verification stable. Across four agentic capabilities and two end-to-end agent benchmarks it retains about 90% of full-context accuracy on average while delivering 1.3–1.7× throughput speedups at 0.2–0.3× the compute cost on isolated text capabilities.

items.title: Beyond Raw Context Transfer: Representation-based Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.title_zh: 超越原始上下文传输：基于表征的联邦检索增强生成
items.summary: FedRepRAG is a decentralized RAG framework that keeps raw documents at their owning clients and exchanges only compact latent representations during cross-client retrieval, using a collaboratively trained projector to turn retrieval embeddings into generator-compatible representation tokens for a frozen LLM or VLM backbone. Across decentralized visual QA and QA benchmarks it consistently beats direct-inference and local-retrieval baselines while substantially reducing retrieval-context length and inference overhead compared with raw-context transfer, though residual representation-level leakage remains.

items.title: FaithSieve: Fine-Grained Evaluation of Math Proofs with Faithful Formal Evidence
items.title_zh: FaithSieve：基于忠实形式化证据的数学证明细粒度评估
items.summary: FaithSieve is a Lean-assisted framework for fine-grained evaluation of natural-language mathematical proofs that decomposes coarse proof steps into local reasoning units, extracts typed proof obligations, and verifies them through a formal evaluation agent gated by semantic alignment scoring. On the 350-problem ProofLoc-Olympiad dataset it reaches 81.43% exact first-error accuracy with a GPT-5.4 backbone versus 72.29% for direct judging, and 84.5% versus 75.0% on the 200-problem ProofLoc-University benchmark.
